title: inset_faces: merge inner verts on shared edges between selected adjacent faces
description:
Analogous to MESH-45 but for the plain inset_faces node (InsetFacesNode.java, @MeshNodeAnnotation id='inset_faces'). The class doc says 'creates inner vertices by lerping each vertex toward the face center' and currently emits 1 inner quad + 4 side quads per selected face unconditionally with fresh inner verts — same per-face-fresh-verts structural issue as coons_inset_faces. When two or more selected faces share an edge, their inner quads end up edge-disconnected. Downstream extrude_mesh(region=true) (the plain, non-coons extrude) cannot form a single connected region from what should be one contiguous inset patch.

Fix direction mirrors MESH-45 flavor A: along shared edges between selected faces, drop both per-face side quads, merge the 2 inner-edge verts into one shared pair along that cage edge, and let inner quads become directly edge-adjacent. At corners where 3+ selected faces meet, the near-corner inner verts from those faces merge into one. Unlike MESH-45, this node does NOT need to keep verts on a Coons surface — it uses flat centroid-lerp placement, so merging can use the standard lerp position (two faces' lerp-to-centroid produce different positions; pick a deterministic rule, likely: place merged vertex at the inset distance along the shared cage edge, i.e. lerp from the shared edge's midpoint/endpoints rather than from each face's centroid).

This ticket should land alongside or after MESH-45 so the two nodes stay behaviorally consistent for the 'select adjacent faces → inset → extrude' pattern.
definition-of-done: 1. Selected cage faces sharing an edge produce one shared pair of inner verts along that edge. 2. At corners with N>=3 selected faces, N near-corner inner verts merge into one. 3. Side quads only emitted on selection-boundary cage edges. 4. Merged inner verts placed deterministically (document the rule in the class javadoc — likely lerp along the shared cage edge, not from face centroids). 5. Downstream extrude_mesh(selection=generated, region=true) produces one connected extrusion per selection-connected-component. 6. Behavior stays consistent with MESH-45's coons variant: same topological structure for the merged output.
testing-plan: 1. Unit: 2x1 grid with both faces selected, inset=0.2. Assert shared inner-edge verts exist (count = 6 inner verts total instead of 8). 2. Unit: 2x2 grid, all 4 selected, inset=0.2. Assert the 4 center-adjacent inner verts collapse to 1 shared vert. 3. Integration: plain inset_faces → plain extrude_mesh(region=true) on adjacent selection produces a single connected region. 4. Parity: for a connected selection, inset_faces topology matches coons_inset_faces topology (same face/vert counts, same adjacency structure); only vertex positions differ (flat lerp vs Coons surface).
